name: Hodaviah
overview: Hodaviah was a male Levite whose descendants are noted for returning to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. His significance is primarily tied to his lineage as part of the tribe of Levi, which was responsible for religious duties in Israel. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodaviah means "give thanks to YHWH," reflecting a theocentric meaning common in Hebrew names. He is also referenced as Hodevah, which carries the same meaning, emphasizing gratitude to God. Additionally, the name Henadad, meaning "favor of Hadad," appears in related contexts but is distinct from Hodaviah.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hodaviah as a descendant of Levi and an ancestor of Jeshua and Kadmiel, linking him to important post-exilic leaders. These relationships are explicitly mentioned, confirming his place within the priestly lineage. Beyond these, no other family connections are detailed.
scriptureSignificance: Hodaviah's importance lies in his role as an ancestor of those who returned to Judah after captivity, highlighting the restoration of the Levitical priesthood and worship in Jerusalem. His lineage connects directly to key figures involved in rebuilding the community and temple worship. Thus, he represents continuity in God's covenant people through the difficult period of exile and return.
